transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been worrying a lot. It jumps from work stuff, like whether this new lab partnership could cost me my position, to whether my data’s wrong, bills piling up, my family thinking I’m falling behind… and grad school. Like I’ve already messed up my chances somehow.
Do you find it hard to control the worrying once it starts?

Yeah… it’s hard to stop. I’ll try to just focus on one thing, like a report or checking an assay, and then one worry kind of sets off another. Before I know it I’m just staring at the screen, thinking through all the ways it could go wrong.
How long have you been worrying like this?
Um… about seven months, I think. It started around when the lab funding changed and that commercial partnership came in. Things just felt different after that.
During these past seven months, have you been worrying like this on most days?
Yeah… most days. It’s kind of always there, jumping between the lab partnership, my data, bills, my family, grad school… stuff like that.
Have you been feeling restless or on edge a lot lately?

Yeah. Mostly at work. I feel kind of wound up, like I can’t really sit still… I’ll tap my foot, check my messages, walk back to the instrument room when I don’t even need to. Even normal lab noises make me jump sometimes.
Have you been getting tired easily lately?
Yeah… I do. Even if I’m in bed the whole night, I wake up feeling like I barely slept. By the time I’m labeling samples or trying to make dinner, I just feel… heavy, and my head feels drained.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

Yeah… I have. I’ll try to just focus on one thing, like a report or checking an assay, but then one worry kicks off another. After a while I’m just staring at the screen, not really taking anything in, thinking through all the ways it could go wrong.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t know… not really depressed, I guess. More just… worn out. It’s hard to tell sometimes.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
Not most days, no. I mean… I get worn down, but I wouldn’t really call it sad.
Do you feel this worrying started because of the changes at work with the lab funding and new partnership?
Yeah… I think so. It kind of started around then, when the funding changed and the commercial partnership came in. It’s been… about seven months now.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot even on days when work isn’t the main thing on your mind?

Yeah… it doesn’t really stay at work. My mind jumps around a lot — like from the lab partnership and whether they’ll cut my position, to if my data’s wrong, bills, my family thinking I’m falling behind… even grad school stuff. It’s kind of constant.
Has this worrying been making it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

Yeah… it has. I missed an internal lab deadline because I just couldn’t get my writing and data review organized. And outside work, even normal stuff — reports, art nights, cooking for my family — it all feels like too much to keep up with.
If the problems at work were suddenly resolved, do you think you would still be worrying this much?

Yeah… I think I probably would. Work is a big part of it, but it doesn’t stop there. My mind just keeps jumping to other things — like whether my data’s wrong, bills, what my family thinks, grad school… it all kind of piles on.
Have you been having a lot of muscle tension lately?

Yeah… mostly in my shoulders and neck. They’re kind of tight all day, and I notice I’m clenching my jaw when I’m staring at spreadsheets. By evening I’ll have a headache and feel stiff, like I’ve been hauling stuff around.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?
I’m… not really sure. My sleep hasn’t been great, I guess, but I don’t know how much to make of it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I mean… maybe a little? I have nights where it’s not great, but I haven’t really been keeping track. So… I’m not sure how to answer that.
Do you feel like your worrying is more than the situation really calls for?

Yeah… probably. I mean, I know some of it is normal stuff to worry about, but my mind keeps jumping around—from the lab partnership and whether my job is going to get cut, to whether my data’s wrong, bills piling up, my family thinking I’m behind… grad school. It feels like I take everything to the worst place pretty fast.
Aside from the work changes, do you feel anxious even when there isn’t any specific stressor going on?

Yeah… it’s not only the work stuff. My mind just kind of jumps around on its own — like if it’s not the lab partnership or whether my position gets cut, then it’s whether my data’s wrong, bills, my family thinking I’m behind… grad school. It’s just sort of constant.
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly a reaction to the changes at work?

Not mainly, no. The work changes are part of it, but… it keeps jumping to other things too — like whether my data’s wrong, bills, my family thinking I’m falling behind, grad school. It feels like it’s more constant than just that one situation.
Do you feel your anxiety would go away if the work situation had never changed?

No… I don’t think so. The work thing is a big part of it, but my mind would probably just latch onto something else — my data being wrong, bills, my family thinking I’m behind, grad school stuff. It’s kind of always jumping around.
